column1: # view document"). A view document declares its figures as data, and a
# declaration is just a map: std/view is the schema for one, so a typo
# is refused at EVALUATION, by unification, rather than by the verb
# that reads the document afterwards. The declaration keys are the view
# options -- the command-line flags without the dashes.
# The source is BUNDLED with the engine (ts/src/std.ts, go/std.go): no
# filesystem, no package resolution, so it is available under every
# include capability except `none`. The two copies are the same bytes,
# and vocabulary-canon and vocabulary-hash below pin that in both
# engines -- they cannot drift without a red suite.
# A declaration that leaves out `out` does not GENERATE, which is how
# the vocabulary makes it required: `aontu view --views` reads the
# declarations out of the generated value, so such a document is
# refused before a figure is drawn -- and a declaration the author
# writes without the vocabulary is refused by the verb instead
# EXPERIMENTAL until the distribution layer can version it by

column3: @"std/view"\nviews: {&: $.view.Figure} & {a: {kind: matrix, order: partition, closure: true, out: "a.txt"}}
